newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank records destroyed in U.S. blaze.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank records destroyed in U.S. blaze.

text.p: One of Switzerland's biggest banks said on Wednesday a U.S. warehouse fire had destroyed some of its old records, but the blaze did not appear to have torched documents that could help the hunt for missing Holocaust wealth.

Credit Suisse Group said the blaze almost totally destroyed a storage depot in Wilkes Barre, Pennsylvania that it and other companies used. It held archives of Credit Suisse's New York branch and of the CS First Boston investment bank.

The bank said in a statement it had asked an accounting firm some months ago to identify files that might be relevant in the search for unclaimed assets of Holocaust victims in Swiss banks, which Jewish groups suspect Swiss banks may be hoarding.
The accounting group took charge of 3,500 files with documents dated 1970 or earlier and removed all those that might shed light on any unclaimed assets, Credit Suisse Group said.

"On the basis of the available information, Credit Suisse Group does not envisage that the investigation into the role of Credit Suisse New York during the Second World War will be affected by the fire...", it said.
Swiss banking giant Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was embarrassed in January when a night watchman discovered it was shredding old documents in violation of a ban on such action.
It called the incident a "regrettable accident" and said no client records were lost.
